findings.reason: parser.ts:1452 only does state.position++ and leaves lineStart at 0. Block indent is state.position - state.lineStart (parser.ts:1243), so a first-line key gets indent 1 while the next key has lineIndent 0. That ends the mapping, and readDocument then throws at parser.ts:1421. The removed skipByteOrderMark also set lineStart.
findings.claim: The leading-BOM skip advances position but not lineStart, so first-line block indent is off by one and multi-key BOM-prefixed mappings fail to parse.
findings.evidence: The removed `skipByteOrderMark` did `state.position++; state.lineStart = state.position`. The replacement is only `if (state.input.charCodeAt(state.position) === 0xFEFF) state.position++`. Block indent is worked out as `state.position - state.lineStart` (lines 1195, 1243, 1257), so a first-line mapping such as `﻿a: 1\nb: 2` starts at indent 1 while `b:` sits at indent 0. The only BOM test (`test/core/units/load-other.test.mjs:7`, `load('﻿foo: bar\n')`) has a single key, so it can't catch this.

findings.reason: skipSeparationSpace (parser.ts:336-337) sets hasSeparation only when position === lineStart or the previous character is whitespace. After the new skip, position is 1, lineStart is 0 and the previous character is 0xFEFF, so the '#' branch at parser.ts:348 never runs.
findings.claim: A comment right after a leading BOM is no longer read as a comment, so valid input like '﻿# comment\nfoo: bar' throws.
findings.evidence: `skipSeparationSpace` treats `#` as a comment only when `hasSeparation` is true. That is computed as `state.position === state.lineStart || isWsOrEol(state.input.charCodeAt(state.position - 1))` (lines 336-337). After the new skip, position is 1 and lineStart is 0, and the previous character is 0xFEFF, which is not whitespace, so the comment branch at line 348 is skipped.

findings.reason: The diff removes testDocumentBoundary and the per-loop skipByteOrderMark. readPlainScalar (parser.ts:776), readBlockScalar (parser.ts:672) and readDocument (parser.ts:1421) now call only testDocumentSeparator, which fails on a 0xFEFF character. A BOM is now stripped only at position 0 (parser.ts:1452).
findings.claim: A BOM before a later document boundary is no longer recognised: plain scalars run across '﻿---' and merge documents, and other boundaries throw 'document separator is expected'.
findings.evidence:
The diff deletes `testDocumentBoundary` and its BOM-prefixed path (`skipByteOrderMark`, then a check for `%` or `---`). It also removes the per-iteration `skipByteOrderMark(state)` from the `parseEvents` loop. Now only position 0 is checked for 0xFEFF. readDocument (line 1421), readPlainScalar (line 776) and readBlockScalar (line 672) test only `testDocumentSeparator` at `lineStart`, so the boundary in `a
...
﻿---
b` hits 'end of the stream or a document separator is expected'. In `foo
﻿---
bar`, the plain scalar is not stopped at the BOM line.
